fix(ui): align subagent avatars with transcript text

Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR adds matching subagent avatars beside transcript names using shared avatar rendering. **Example:** A conversation launches 12 subagents, including map personal and map agents. - **Before:** The transcript shows names and “10 more,” while colored avatars appear only in Details. - **After:** The first two transcript names have avatars matching their Details colors. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The visual behavior is directly demonstrated and the implementation is focused, but the attributable CSS budget failure blocks readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected the published clean and annotated browser comparisons from the fixture-backed Gateway: the changed transcript renderer displays matching avatars beside the first two names in a 12-subagent summary; this proves the visual change, without claiming a live model run. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Users tracking several subagents must match transcript names to colored avatars elsewhere in the UI. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction adds a clear visual cue using existing identities and preserves the compact summary and interactions. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep this PR open: the maintainer-authored visual improvement is useful and demonstrated, but its CSS growth causes a required CI failure. **Priority:** P3 **Reviewed head:** `d6a44148c2561702b2fa7a67e3cb5399a68cd801` ## Before merge - [ ] **\[P2\] Keep the avatar styling within the enforced CSS budget (P2)** - The added styling makes the paired `control-ui-performance` check fail: total raw CSS grows from 1,748,937 to 1,749,182 bytes (+245), while an already-over-budget base permits only 64 bytes of build variance. The existing ceiling overrun is inherited, but this additional growth causes the failure and consequently blocks `openclaw/ci-gate`. Consolidate or reuse the avatar/name styles to meet the existing allowance, then rerun the paired comparison. ## Findings - [P2] [P2] Keep the avatar styling within the enforced CSS budget — `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagent-badge.css:18-23`
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Control UI turns recorded tool activity and child-session identities into transcript summaries, disclosures, and session-navigation buttons. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Recorded tool activity] --> B[Launch and stop presentation] B --> C[Transcript names] D[Child session keys] --> E[Shared avatar badge] E --> C E --> F[Details subagent roster] C --> G[Existing session navigation] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the shared avatar presentation and consolidate its styling until the paired CSS budget check passes. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? This is an enhancement; the inspected before/after browser captures directly establish the visual difference without executing target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The shared badge is justified by its Details and transcript consumers, preserves the existing identity hash, and removes the replaced avatar styling; only the demonstrated CSS budget failure needs repair. Full review comments: - [P2] [P2] Keep the avatar styling within the enforced CSS budget — `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-subagent-badge.css:18-23` The added styling makes the paired `control-ui-performance` check fail: total raw CSS grows from 1,748,937 to 1,749,182 bytes (+245), while an already-over-budget base permits only 64 bytes of build variance. The existing ceiling overrun is inherited, but this additional growth causes the failure and consequently blocks `openclaw/ci-gate`. Consolidate or reuse the avatar/name styles to meet the existing allowance, then rerun the paired comparison. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.96 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [6447b3e8c29e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6447b3e8c29e90f2c43878ef6492ca905c9e1a93). ### Provenance checked - `Details avatar colors and status badges` keeps the original intent (4a65c3a4d6b018cb4d3487436eb30448a9a4455b: Provide compact subagent summaries with separate child navigation; later palette and radius changes established the existing appearance.) - `Shared UTF-16 identity hash` keeps the original intent (2c67718f1967bcfa79ff8aac7a4806d2b133190d: Remove the duplicate UI hash while preserving existing identity hues and hash values.) - `Compact lifecycle summaries and launch links` keeps the original intent (18136c960eaf70cac7ee083959c55d13d159afc2: Present chronological launch and stop facts with stable disclosures and recorded child identities.) - `Deferred detailed tool rendering` keeps the original intent (2c5b726de0e978c4c05ec5fc06dcce422f3ef21b: Keep detailed tool parsing and rendering outside the eager chat boot path.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm ui:check-performance:base ee37dd3b03358775b84d5ce2f04e6de8335dd082 - pnpm --dir ui test run src/pages/chat/components/chat-details-subagents.test.tsx src/pages/chat/components/chat-activity-disclosure.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-spawned-subagent.test.ts - pnpm lint:ui:styles - git diff --check What I checked: - **Pinned change and current-main context:** The introduced diff shares the existing Details avatar rendering with transcript summaries and expanded launch rows; the existing affected files are unchanged between the merge base and fetched main.
